verdict.rationale: Marqeta documents its own spend controls covering most of this story: authorization controls restrict a card's user to a single merchant, and velocity controls cap both spend amount and transaction count over a time span. JIT funding also lets the developer's system approve or deny each authorization with its own rules, which could enforce an exact amount. However, no documented single-use card type or automatic deactivation after first use appears, so the developer must combine several controls to get this behaviour. Missing for 10: an explicit single-use/burner card feature, documented exact-amount matching, documentation that the card is invalidated after first use, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can issue single-use and tightly scoped cards — one purchase, one merchant, an exact amount — so a leaked number is worthless the moment it's used

citations.quote: Limit where a user can make transactions to a single merchant or group of merchants.
You can configure velocity controls to limit how much users can spend and the number of transactions they can make in a given span of time.
Your system receives funding requests and approves or denies them using your own business rules.
Virtual card issuance: Create instant-issue virtual cards that are ready for immediate use.
